$why: The diff reviewers' half of the detective's 'shared' finding (team-lead-review and
code-review-cycle, through lib/review-criteria.sh). Full consumer review 2026-10-02: neither
reviewer was shown it, so a required manifest bump read as a thin change and a saved local-path
redirection to a sibling's working copy would have read as a fix. Locations are RELATIVE.

Operator, 2026-10-06: a consumer's declared range is never changed by a story ('avoid package.json upgrades in this change'; a range may be locked for a reason); the provider ships the change on a release line inside each consumer's range.
description: Appended to the criteria a diff reviewer judges against when the detective reported a shared fix site: what is shared, where the sibling working copies are, and what a correct shared change looks like in a diff.
body:
SHARED WITH OTHER CODELINES OF THIS STORY — the investigation reported:
__SHARED_SITES__
The other codelines' working copies, relative to this codeline's root:
__SIBLING_LOCATIONS__
Judge the diff with this in mind. A change to this codeline's declared range of a shared package is a BLOCKER finding: the range belongs to this codeline's own upgrade decisions, never to this story — where the range does not take the change, the provider ships it on a release line inside the range. A dependency pointed at another codeline's working copy (a local path or link) that is SAVED in the diff is a defect: that is how the change is built and tested, not part of what ships. Where this codeline provides the package, judge whether each consumer above receives the change through the range it ALREADY declares, on every release line those ranges require; a consumer left out of reach is a blocker.
